title: Office and Technology
summary: Basic workplace objects, devices, and simple actions around technology.
whyItMatters: Office and technology vocabulary helps you manage simple tasks at work, in class, and at home. With a small set of devices, documents, and actions, you can describe what you have, what you need, and where a basic problem occurs.

mentalModel.title: Build a desk scene
mentalModel.content: Picture one workspace and place each noun in it: computer, screen, keyboard, telephone, paper, pen, and printer.

mentalModel.title: Connect every device to an action
mentalModel.content: Technology words become useful when paired with verbs: den Computer benutzen, eine E-Mail schreiben, ein Dokument drucken.

mentalModel.title: Separate object, task, and problem
mentalModel.content: Describe what the thing is, what you do with it, and whether it works: 'Das ist der Drucker. Ich drucke ein Dokument. Der Drucker funktioniert nicht.'

ruleBlocks.title: Learn devices with article and plural
ruleBlocks.content: Keep the noun package intact: der Computer – die Computer, die Tastatur – die Tastaturen, das Handy – die Handys.

ruleBlocks.title: Pair objects with common actions
ruleBlocks.content: Build useful combinations such as 'eine E-Mail schreiben', 'ein Dokument öffnen', and 'den Drucker benutzen'.

ruleBlocks.title: Describe a problem simply
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'funktioniert nicht', 'ist kaputt', or 'geht nicht' to signal that a device or process has a problem.

sentenceStructure: Use 'haben' to state what is available and 'brauchen' to state what is needed.
Use a direct object after many technology actions: 'Ich öffne das Dokument.'
Place 'nicht' near the problem description: 'Der Drucker funktioniert nicht.'
Use short separate sentences when describing a task and its problem.

concepts: name common devices and office objects
give instructions and make workplace requests
explain technical problems in more detail
coordinate tasks and solutions at work

comparisons.summary: This theme provides the objects and situations. The grammar lesson distinguishes having no object from an action or device not working.
The communication lesson helps when a device name, spelling, or instruction is not understood.

examples.de: Auf dem Schreibtisch sind ein Computer, eine Tastatur und ein Handy.
examples.en: There are a computer, a keyboard, and a mobile phone on the desk.

examples.de: Bitte öffnen und speichern Sie das Dokument.
examples.en: Please open and save the document.

examples.de: Ich brauche Papier und einen Stift.
examples.en: I need paper and a pen.

commonMistakes.reason: 'Handy' is a German noun for a mobile phone, not the English adjective.
'E-Mail' is normally feminine in standard German.

commonMistakes.correct: Learn: der Drucker – drucken – funktioniert nicht.
commonMistakes.reason: An object is easier to use and remember when connected to an action and a common situation.

specialCases: Technology vocabulary changes quickly and often includes international loanwords.
'Der Rechner' can also mean computer, while 'der Computer' is widely understood.
'Geht nicht' is an informal general problem phrase; 'funktioniert nicht' is clearer for devices.
tips: Label the devices and objects in your real workspace.
Practice one positive and one negative sentence for each device.
Describe a simple digital task as three actions in order.

memoryHooks.title: One desk, many words
memoryHooks.content: Place every new object on one mental desk and imagine using it.

memoryHooks.title: Object, action, problem
memoryHooks.content: For each device, learn what it is, what you do with it, and one way to say it is not working.
